The Engineering Delivery and Defect Analytics (EDDA) project combines software work-item records, code-change metadata,
continuous-integration (CI) build results, automated test outcomes and production incident records. The objective is to understand
engineering delivery quality and estimate whether a completed work item is associated with a production defect within 30 days of
release.
The raw synthetic dataset contains 12,000 work-item observations from 24 repositories and 8 engineering teams. After duplicate
removal, exclusion of records with invalid release timestamps and target-label validation, 11,760 observations remain for analysis.
Of these, 1,176 are labelled as having a production defect within 30 days, giving a positive prevalence of 10.0%.

Code coverage measures the proportion of code executed during testing, focusing on how much of the actual code (lines, branches, conditions) has been tested, while test coverage measures how well the test suite covers the features of the software, asking whether the right things the user cares about are being tested. Code coverage is quantitative and tool-driven, focusing on what code was executed, but does not confirm whether the logic was validated correctly. Test coverage is qualitative and harder to measure, focusing on whether requirements, user flows, edge cases, and risk areas are actually being tested.
